subject: OneTrust: KMS-signed evidence & hashchain proof
messages:
From: Lena Morales <lena.morales@greengrid.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@greengrid.com
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence signing requirements for CAIQ upload

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for taking this on. As part of our procurement policy and our security team's CAIQ validation, we need artifacts that prove authenticity and provenance for the evidence you upload to OneTrust. Specifically: 

- A SHA256 manifest of each artifact, plus a KMS/HSM-signed digest (PKCS7 or similar) for the manifest.
- Timestamps for when each object was uploaded to your storage (S3) including object version ID and server-side encryption metadata.
- A simple verification instruction (1-2 paragraphs) we can run to confirm the signature and the matching object versions.

I've attached our request template (greensight-request-template.xlsx) showing the fields the GreenGrid reviewers will check. Can you confirm that Redwood can provide the signed digests (not just hashes) and that you'll include S3 version metadata? If not, tell me what alternatives you can provide (e.g., signed hashchain entries, notarization).

We'd like to review a sample proof bundle by EOD Wednesday so our security team can mark the CAIQ as "evidence accepted" in OneTrust.

-Lena
Security Reviewer, GreenGrid

Attachment: greensight-request-template.xlsx (Excel template listing required fields and sample checks)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Morales <lena.morales@greengrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence signing requirements for CAIQ upload

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear checklist and the template. Looping in Aditya (security infra) and Ben (vendor intake) to coordinate.

We can provide a KMS-signed manifest and S3 metadata; here's the proposed minimal plan so you know exactly what we'll upload and how to verify:

1) For each artifact (PDF, JSON, CAIQ fragment) we compute SHA256 and add an entry to a single manifest.jsonl (one line per artifact: filename, sha256, s3_key, s3_version, timestamp).
2) We sign the manifest with an AWS CloudHSM-backed key using PKCS7 detached signature. The output is manifest.jsonl.sig (Base64/DER).
3) We store the artifacts and manifest in a versioned S3 bucket with SSE-KMS; object metadata will include x-amz-version-id and x-amz-server-side-encryption. We will include the KMS Key ID used to sign in the manifest header.
4) We will upload the manifest + signature + a short verification.txt (two commands: sha256sum check + openssl cms -verify invocation) into OneTrust as a single zip named greengrid-proof-yyyyMMdd.zip.

Timeline: Aditya estimates we can produce a sample bundle within 36 hours after you confirm the fields in your template. Ben will schedule the OneTrust upload and mapping.

Next steps: Aditya, can you confirm the signing key (CloudHSM alias) and paste the verification commands you'll include? Ben, can you open the OneTrust record and tell us which fields we must populate so the upload hits the correct evidence type?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Vendor Security Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Morales <lena.morales@greengrid.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence signing requirements for CAIQ upload

Quick technical note on the signing flow — confirming we can do the PKCS7 detached signature from a CloudHSM-backed key and include the S3 version metadata. Steps I'll run: 

- Use a transient EC keypair stored in AWS CloudHSM (alias: alias/rw-kms-evidence-2027). We'll call into the HSM via an ephemeral signing job to avoid long-lived app keys.
- Script (kms-sign-script.sh) will: compute sha256 for each file, append entries to manifest.jsonl, upload objects with SSE-KMS and versioning enabled, then call a signing wrapper that produces manifest.jsonl.sig (PKCS7 detached).
- Verification snippet we'll include as verification.txt: 
  1) sha256sum -c manifest.jsonl 
  2) openssl cms -verify -inform DER -in manifest.jsonl.sig -content manifest.jsonl -CAfile /path/to/rw-root.pem -out /dev/null
  3) Compare S3 x-amz-version-id reported in manifest to the live object metadata via aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-evidence --key "<s3_key>" --version-id "<version>"

Risk/control note: generating and signing proofs touches a KMS/HSM key. We should route this through Alice (control owner) for SOC 2 attestation that this workflow is acceptable. I can draft a short control note.

Attachment: kms-sign-script.sh (bash script stub showing hashing, upload, sign sequence)

I'll prepare the sample bundle today and post a test link.

-Aditya
Senior Security Engineer
